width.$description: The width a toast takes in the viewport on a screen wide enough for a corner: about 45 characters of body text per line, narrow enough to leave the page readable beside it, wide enough for a title, a sentence and one action. On a screen narrower than it, a toast spans the viewport less its gutter instead. A content-measure constraint with no home on any primitive scale (the spacing scale tops out at 8rem), so it is a component token, like tooltip.max-width.

peek.$description: How far each older toast shows beyond the one in front of it while a fanned stack is collapsed (`stack="fan"`): enough of its edge to read as another toast behind, little enough that the stack stays about one toast tall. The same value as `space.3`, named for what it measures so the stack can be tuned on its own without moving every gap that uses that step.

scale-step.$description: How much smaller each older toast is drawn than the one in front of it while a fanned stack is collapsed, per step of depth: a unitless amount taken off a scale of 1. Small enough that a toast two steps back is still its own width to the eye, large enough that the layers read as receding. A ratio with no scale of its own, so it is a component token.
